requirement: If every `vet_answer` callback invoked by {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer` returns `Ok(VetResult::Accept)`, or the request has no callbacks, the answer is successfully submitted and the agent conversation ends.
rationale:
The subject `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer.ok` has two obligations. The first is that when every callback returns `Accept`, the answer is submitted successfully and the conversation ends. The second is that the same holds when the request has no callbacks. Both are covered.

**All callbacks accept.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[vetting_collects_corrections_and_rechecks_every_callback]` registers three callbacks, one before `contents_of_current_node()` and two after it, so both builder phases are exercised.
- On the second submission (`true`) all three callbacks return `Accept`. The first accepts unconditionally. The second accepts because the answer is `true`. The third accepts because its one-shot flag was already consumed.
- The test asserts `.await.unwrap()` yields `true`, which is the successful submission.
- It asserts `requests.len() == 2`, so no further agent request is made after the all-accept round. This shows the conversation ended.
- `seen == [false, true]` shows the first callback ran on both submissions.

**No callbacks.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[one_submission_accepts_only_its_value_and_skips_other_calls_and_prose]` makes a plain `ctx.ask::<bool>()` with no `vet_answer` callbacks. It asserts the awaited result is `Ok(false)`, the submitted value. It also asserts exactly one provider request was made, so the conversation ended after acceptance.

**Obligations delegated elsewhere.** Callback ordering, `Err` handling and correction feedback belong to the parent `vet_answer` requirement and to `vet_answer.corrections`. They are not part of this subject. Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

I found no scenario within the subject's text that the tests would accept incorrectly.
